persons.name: WallStDiaries
persons.digest: Wall Street Diaries tracked the selloff that erased the post-election rally: Nasdaq 100 down as much as 5.6%, roughly $2 trillion lost in tech. On **Nvidia** it relayed that China has not approved import of 600,000 H200 chips and George Noble's Cisco analogy. It also posted **Bloom Energy**'s 900 MW NTT DATA deal, **Micron** suspending its $4.5 billion Taiwan fab, **Oracle** cancelling a $7 billion Tencent deal and **JPMorgan** falling on the Epstein agenda. On macro, US jobless claims fell to 189,000 and Iran risk stood out for oil.

persons.name: wallstengine
persons.digest: Wall St Engine relayed the global selloff in numbers: Nikkei fell 6.2% into a bear market and South Korea's market lost nearly half its value in four months. Per WSJ **Anthropic**'s annualized revenue run rate topped $80 billion in October but its IPO raise may shrink from $100 billion to about $80 billion. In after-hours moves **Cloudflare** rose 18% and **Airbnb** 11% while **DraftKings** fell 19% and **Atlassian** 17%; **Sony** beat estimates and raised guidance. It also shared that **Tesla** will wind down Cybertruck production in the middle of next year.
